nodes.label: Circuit Breaker (Payment Hub)
nodes.rationale: Circuit breaker auto-disconnects a faulty Connector when error/timeout exceeds threshold, preventing cascade failures across other Connectors and Core.

nodes.label: Idempotency Key Pattern
nodes.rationale: Idempotency key in API header prevents duplicate transaction creation on network retries. Critical for payment systems where duplicate charges must be prevented.

nodes.label: Vault/KMS Secret Management
nodes.rationale: API keys and secrets stored in Vault/KMS (not in code or config files) to prevent credential exposure. Connectors fetch secrets at runtime.

nodes.label: Webhook Engine
nodes.rationale: Exponential backoff retry (1min, 5min, 15min, 1h, 6h) for up to 5 attempts on webhook failure. HMAC-SHA256 signature in X-Signature header ensures integrity.

nodes.label: Payment Hub System
nodes.rationale: Centralized payment middleware that abstracts multiple PSPs behind a single API. BizOne POS/Website/Mobile call one API instead of integrating each payment partner directly, enabling easier PSP addition.

nodes.label: Connector Plugin Architecture
nodes.rationale: Plugin-based design allows adding new PSPs without modifying Core Payment Hub code (zero-core-change). Each Connector implements a standard interface contract; hot-plug enables activation without restart.

nodes.label: Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) Pattern
nodes.rationale: Separate API gateways per client type (mobile, web, partner) allow each to expose an optimized view of backend services without polluting a single shared gateway with client-specific logic.

nodes.label: mTLS and Service Identity
nodes.rationale: Identity is based on service account, not network address. mTLS encrypts traffic but must be paired with explicit AuthorizationPolicy rules (default deny, explicit allow).

nodes.label: Architecture Pattern Decision Tree
nodes.rationale: Select architecture based on team size, bounded contexts, event-driven needs, load patterns, and consistency requirements. Conway's Law: architecture mirrors org structure.

nodes.label: BizOne Platform
nodes.rationale: All-in-One platform for SME retail management in Vietnam, targeting omni-channel sales. Built on NextJS + MariaDB to unify POS, inventory, CRM, reporting, and sales channels on one platform.

nodes.label: BizOne Technology Stack
nodes.rationale: NextJS 14+ App Router + MariaDB chosen for type-safe full-stack development. Redis for session/cache, BullMQ for async sync with e-commerce platforms, Docker for containerized multi-tenant deployment.

nodes.label: Dual Screen POS Architecture
nodes.rationale: Two-screen POS design: employee screen for operations and customer-facing display. Customer screen shows cart, totals, discounts, QR code. Improves transparency and speeds up payment.

nodes.label: Multi-Tenant Architecture
nodes.rationale: Each tenant gets isolated database/schema to prevent data leakage between customers. Required for SaaS model serving multiple independent retail businesses.

nodes.norm_label: transaction state machine (created → pending → success/failed/expired → refunded)

nodes.label: Transactional Outbox Pattern
nodes.rationale: Write to database and outbox table atomically to guarantee at-least-once event delivery even if the broker is temporarily unavailable.

nodes.label: Saga Pattern for Distributed Transactions
nodes.rationale: Saga coordinates multi-service workflows via event choreography or orchestration; compensation transactions handle rollback when a step fails.

nodes.label: Audit Log System (BizOne)
nodes.rationale: Append-only audit log records all critical operations (CRUD, payments, config changes) for fraud prevention. Stored minimum 90 days with IP, device, user, and before/after data.

nodes.label: Offline POS Mode
nodes.rationale: POS stores transactions locally when internet connection is lost (localStorage), syncs when connectivity is restored. Critical for physical retail where network outages must not halt sales.

nodes.label: BroadcastChannel API for POS Sync
nodes.rationale: BroadcastChannel API or WebSocket chosen to sync employee and customer POS screens in real-time. Supports two browser tabs or two physical monitors.

nodes.label: Brainstorm-Explore-Plan-Critique-Build Process
nodes.rationale: Two-pass process: first build a compact token system (color, type, layout, signature), then self-critique against brief before coding to avoid AI-design clichés.

nodes.label: Frontend Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Typography carries personality; structure is information; motion should be deliberate; restraint and self-critique ensure distinctive but disciplined design outcomes.
